title: Remote provider ignores its not-ready state when analyzing images
reasoning: The provider advertises enabled/is_ready as false when health checks have marked _ready false, but analyze_image gates only on _enabled and still sends requests to the remote OCR endpoint. Callers that rely on enabled or is_ready to represent provider availability can observe the provider as unavailable while analyze_image continues to make network calls and potentially mutate _ready back to true. That makes readiness semantics inconsistent and can route work to a provider that failed health.
reproduction: After health_check catches a timeout and sets _ready=False, enabled and is_ready both return False. A subsequent analyze_image call still posts to /ocr/analyze because it checks only _enabled.
recommendation: Either make analyze_image enforce readiness by checking self.enabled/is_ready and raising ProviderRequestError when not ready, or explicitly document and rename the readiness semantics so failed health is advisory and request success may recover the provider.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included test file covers only local OcrService helpers and CUDA fallback behavior; it has no RemoteHttpOcrProvider readiness or health-failure tests.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a remote provider test with a mocked client where health_check times out, then assert analyze_image does not issue a POST and raises a ProviderRequestError while _ready is false.
minimumFixScope: Update RemoteHttpOcrProvider.analyze_image readiness guard and add focused tests for health failure followed by analyze_image.
